title: Developer Sandbox Cost Estimator — Release Notes 1.0
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
=======

Release: Developer Sandbox Cost Estimator v1.0
Date: 2026-10-30 (GA) — patch 2026-11-05
Owners: Product (Maya Chen), Eng: dev-tools (Evan Kline), Integrations (Luis Ortega)
Status: GA / gradual rollout to all orgs over two weeks

Intro
-----
This release ships the Developer Sandbox Cost Estimator (DSCE) v1.0: an offline and lightweight online estimator for modeling per-route and per-workload cost and latency at development time. DSCE is designed for engineers to iterate on prompt design, model variant choices, and routing policies without incurring production tokens or warm-capacity consumption.

Key objectives addressed
- Allow developers to get realistic cost+latency estimates for common workloads inside the Developer Sandbox and CLI.
- Provide a stable SDK and an online /v1/cost-estimate API for programmatic integration with onboarding flows and CI checks.
- Reduce onboarding churn and billing surprises during hosted->dedicated migration by surfacing fidelity and quantization trade-offs early.

What’s included in 1.0
- CLI: redwood dsce init / simulate / compare — local-mode and remote-mode (uses low-cost preview instances).
- SDK: Python and TypeScript packages with simulation harness and built-in workload templates (chat, summarization, embedding-heavy).
- Online API: POST /v1/cost-estimate \- JSON input schema and response with per-token breakdowns, KV-cache hit simulation, batching impact, and confidence bands.
- Console UX: "Cost Preview" panel in Developer Playground for sandbox accounts (UI opt-in via the top-right sandbox toggle).
- Telemetry: new events (dsce.simulate.start, dsce.simulate.complete, dsce.api.estimate) and attribution fields to connect estimates to onboarding experiments.
- Guardrails: default SLO for estimator uptime 99.5% (sandbox tier), latency budget 200ms p95 for the online API.

Compatibility & Supported Scenarios
- Works for hosted and dedicated-variant simulations. Private (VPC) customers can run the CLI local-mode using on-prem weights and an agent that simulates capacity knobs (see section "Private deployment notes").
- Models: supports all catalog models plus quantized variants; estimation accuracy is highest for models with verified performance profiles in the catalog.

API reference (summary)
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/cost-estimate\- Auth: Bearer token (same scope as developer sandbox: scope dsce:estimate)\- Request (JSON):
  {
    "model": "string (model-id)",
    "input_shape": "{messages:[{role:...}], tokens_avg:int}",
    "workload_profile": "chat|completion|embeddings|reranking",
    "batching": "none|auto|manual",
    "kv_cache_prefix_tokens": "int",
    "quantization": "none|int8|int4",
    "sim_options": "{warmup_steps:int, sample_count:int}"
  }
- Response (JSON summary):
  {
    "estimated_total_tokens": "int",
    "token_cost_usd": "float",
    "inference_cost_usd": "float",
    "estimated_latency_ms_p95": "int",
    "kv_cache_hit_pct": "float",
    "confidence_interval_pct": "float"
  }

Example CLI usage
1) Quick local estimate:
   $ redwood dsce simulate --model redwood-v1 --profile chat --input examples/checkout_flow.json

2) Compare variants:
   $ redwood dsce compare --baseline redwood-v1 --variant redwood-v1-quant --workload chat --output diffs.csv

Accuracy & SLOs
- Target estimator accuracy: within ±10% of real production unit economics for typical dev workloads (chat/completion with median length <512 tokens) on models with catalog-verified profiles.
- Online API latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for sandbox fleet; availability SLO: 99.5%.
- Rate limits: sandbox default 100 rps per org for /v1/cost-estimate; CLI local-mode only constrained by host.

Rollout plan
1) Canary (2026-10-30): 10% of sandbox orgs — telemetry + internal QA.
2) Gradual 50% (2026-11-02): enable CLI remote-mode for beta program orgs and surface UX in Playground for invited users.
3) GA (2026-11-05): enable for all sandbox orgs; default opt-in for new signups.

Migration & adoption guidance
- Developer adoption checklist (recommended):
  1. Add dsce:estimate scope to CI job that runs cost checks on PRs.
  2. Use the compare CLI in a pre-merge job to detect >15% cost regressions.
  3. Link estimation results to performance tests: store dsce outputs as artifact for traceability.

- Customer migration note: Existing consumption-advisor connectors remain the source of truth for billed amounts. DSCE outputs are advisory; customers should continue to validate against warm-capacity and real-run invoices prior to contractual negotiation.

Private deployment notes
- Customers on Private: ship CLI local-mode with an optional on-prem simulator agent. Configure simulator via YAML at /etc/redwood/dsce/simulator.yaml (example below). The agent uses local kernel profiles and does not send data to Redwood public services by default.

Example simulator.yaml (ASCII table representation):
+----------------------+---------------------------+-----------------+
| field                | description               | example value   |
+----------------------+---------------------------+-----------------+
| catalog_profiles_dir  | local path to model proft | /opt/redwood/profiles |
| warmup_steps         | number of internal warmup | 25              |
| sample_count         | Monte Carlo runs          | 50              |
| allow_telemetry      | send non-PII telemetry    | false           |
+----------------------+---------------------------+-----------------+

Known issues & limitations
- Estimator currently underestimates costs for multi-model pipelined workflows by up to 18% when KV cache reuse is large — we plan to address in 1.1 with a cross-model KV coordination model.
- Embedding-heavy batch scenarios with >10k tokens per batch may return wider confidence intervals; increase sample_count in sim_options to tighten bands.

Security & data handling
- Sandbox mode is opt-in and estimator runtime strips PII from sample inputs by default.
- Telemetry events exclude raw prompts; they contain workload fingerprints (hashes) and aggregated metrics. Customers running local-mode can opt out of telemetry in simulator.yaml.

Telemetry & monitoring
- New telemetry events and tags:
  - dsce.simulate.start / dsce.simulate.complete (tags: model_id, workload_profile, org_id)
  - dsce.api.estimate (tags: model_family, quantization, batching_mode)
- Dashboards: Product -> Developer Tools -> DSCE Overview (new) shows estimator accuracy vs production, adoption by org, and CI failure rates for cost regression checks.

Operational runbook (high-level)
1. On alert (estimator_p95_latency > 250ms sustained for 10m): escalate to dev-tools oncall, route to canary rollback group.\2. For accuracy regressions (>20% delta vs production): create incident with severity P2 and notify product.

Post-release roadmap (1.1 & 1.2 highlights)
- 1.1 (Q1 2027): multi-model pipeline estimation, tighter KV reuse model, improved embedding batch accuracy.
- 1.2 (Q2 2027): SLO-driven estimator suggestions in Console, merchant-grade SLA for dedicated customers, and a plugins API for custom cost factors.
